title: 4th Workshop of the Political Economy Working Group — Programme
text:

Below is the programme of the workshop.

title: Zoé Evrard
text:
Position: Postdoctoral Researcher at UCLouvain
My research focuses on the political economy of planning and neoliberalism in non-majoritarian contexts. My thesis analysed the redeployment of macroeconomic planning in Belgium from the 1970s to the 1990s, and forms the basis of my current book project. I am also studying Belgian neoliberalism (including the early neoliberal movement, interprofessional industrial relations since 1996, as well as the negotiated character of the Belgian trajectory of change), and development banking (particularly the federal SFPIM). I am currently developing a new research project that extends my work on planning, expertise and neoliberalisation to the European level.

Position: Assistant Professor at ICHEC Brussels Management School
I am a financial market sociologist. I have worked on various decision-making devices used by market professionals (stock market indices, Bloomberg Terminal…). I am currently interested in the role of investment fund managers in capital allocation, particularly “passive” and “green” funds.

title: Belgian Political Economy Working Group
text:
Research areas
The field of political economy provides key analytical tools for understanding a range of fundamental issues in our societies, such as the regulation of globalised economic systems, financial crises, inequalities and tensions between capitalism, ecology and democracy. The diversity of research topics and the theoretical and methodological pluralism of this disciplinary field enable constant dialogue with other fields of political science and other social science disciplines (economics, geography, sociology, anthropology, etc.). In Belgium, a group of researchers are developing various research projects in political economy.
The members of the Belgian Political Economy Working Group are working on a wide range of topics, including: the political economy of the Green transition; the political economy of central banks and financialisation; the role of the state in the economy; the circulation of ideas and expertise, across international and domestic political arenas; neoliberalism and neoliberalisation; the political economy of the European Union; the political economy of development and globalisation; etc.
The group organises regular workshops and promotes the visibility of political economy research in Belgium.
The Belgian Political Economy Working Group is institutionalised through a “Working Group” of the Association Belge Francophone de Science Politique (ABSP). The coordinators are Tom Duterme, Zoé Evrard, Ariane Gemander and Tiago Moreira Ramalho.
It is also a “Groupe de Contact” of the FNRS. The president of the contact group is Clément Fontan and the secretary is Ariane Gemander.

title: Belgian Political Economy Working Group
text:
Get Involved
If you are interested in being involved in the Belgian Political Economy Working Group, don’t hesitate to join our regular events. We also have a mailing list to share news and information about our activities. You can subscribe to the mailing list by sending an email to any of the coordinators of the working group: Tom Duterme, Zoé Evrard, Ariane Gemander and Tiago Moreira Ramalho.

title: Ariane Gemander
text:
Position: PhD Student and Teaching Assistant at ULB
I am a political scientist working on public finance reforms in European states in contexts of crisis. My thesis focuses on the IMF interventions in Bulgaria in the 1990s and in Greece after the 2008 crisis from a political sociology approach. I also specialized in discourse analysis methodologies.

title: 6th Workshop of the Political Economy Working Group — Call for Papers
text:
The Political Economy Working Group is pleased to invite you to a workshop on Friday, 19 June 2026, at ICHEC Brussels. Founded during the ABSP Congress in February 2024, this group aims to contribute to the advancement and growth of the field of political economy in Belgium.
The workshop will be divided into two parts:
Contributions are welcome in either French or English. Presentations should generally be delivered in English.
Organizers: Tom Duterme (ICHEC), Ariane Gemander (ULB), Aurélien Goutsmedt (UCLouvain & ICHEC)

title: 6th Workshop of the Political Economy Working Group — Call for Papers
text:
Next steps
To propose a presentation for the morning or afternoon sessions, send a title and abstract of no more than 400 words to Aurélien Goutsmedt and Ariane Gemander by April 10, 2026. If you wish to present in the PhD morning session, please indicate this clearly in your submission.
Notification of acceptance will be sent by April 17, 2026.
Manuscripts (working papers, chapters, or drafts) will be requested by June 8, 2026, in order to give discussants and other participants sufficient time to prepare. We recommend manuscripts of between 5,000 and 10,000 words.
